result.summary:
VERDICT: doc-only correction, route to ORCH -- not new design or implementation work. This re-confirms, from a fresh read of all primary sources (not by trusting the prior run's report alone), the same conclusion ISSUE-FIXER already reached in WF03-ISS0402-20260902 (recorded in ISS-0402.yaml's own scoping_note): the originally-cited blocker is genuinely gone, but an independent, already-on-record, stronger reason survives untouched, so no code change is warranted.

(1) CONFIRMED join_counters persistence gap is closed. Fresh grep of lib/letflow/engine.ex (current HEAD 1d8ee6cc, fetched/verified against origin/main -- not a stale checkout, learning explicitly applied from ISS-0397's own false_alarm_note about exactly this trap) shows join_counters is now persisted unconditionally on every write path: insert_instance_projection/8 (~line 1274, create/2's own M1 insert) and the shared post-transition write site (~line 1502, 'join_counters is persisted unconditionally on every call (ISS-0397 fix...)'), and correctly deserialized on read (~line 2167, build_instance_state/3, SnapshotWriter.deserialize_join_counters/1). No hardcoded join_counters: %{} remains anywhere in cancel_instance/3's call graph.

(2) OQ-2's text does NOT name join-counters persistence as its sole reason once section 4 (not just the one summary line at line 608) is read in full. Section 4 (req052-instance-cancellation.md:273-347) gives the persistence gap as the PROXIMATE reason wiring {:cancel_branch,_} would be a no-op today, but section 0's 2026-08-22 update (lines 111-134, citing ISS-0098/GH#326) independently verified against R-Co's actual shipped source (R-Co/src/engine/instance.zig, cancelInstance, EE-08, lines 2513-2634) that R-Co's own reference cancellation algorithm (its own doc-commented 8-step sequence, steps d/e) issues plain unconditional SQL UPDATEs on tasks/timers directly inside one transaction -- it never drives per-branch events through R-Co's own transition/graph machinery AT ALL, persistence gap or not. This is architectural PARITY with the reference system, not a stopgap for a missing table. ISS-0098 predates ISS-0397 by over a week and was never touched by it.

(3) Confirmed via grep across lib/letflow_web/, docs/uat/, docs/requirements.yaml (re-run fresh, same as the 20260902 pass) that no route, controller, or UAT scenario needs branch-level cancellation as a caller-facing feature today; requirements REQ-051/052/053/054 are all status: done with no deferred follow-up naming it. dispatch_cancel_branch/3 (lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex) is exercised only by direct unit tests of Transition itself, never by any real caller path.

(4) Two non-trivial semantic questions remain genuinely unresolved with zero reference-implementation precedent to draw from (R-Co has no branch-scoped cancel mode to consult): how already-completed sibling branches of the same split should be handled when one branch is cancelled (does the join fire short, or get suppressed), and whether cancelling a branch that spawned a REQ-062 SUB_PROCESS child should cascade to that child (req062's own EE-08 no-cascade answer is reasoned for whole-instance cancel only and does not transfer). These require a product decision via a new requirement (REQ-ANALYST/REQ-VALIDATOR), not something ISSUE-FIXER or CODE-DESIGNER can improvise inside a bugfix issue.

CONCLUSION: this is case (a) from the task framing -- OQ-2's own text (specifically its section-0 update) already states the real, independent, still-valid reason (R-Co parity, ISS-0098), so the actual fix here is small and doc-only: correct req052-instance-cancellation.md's section-4/section-11 OQ-2 framing so it leads with the R-Co-parity reason rather than reading as if join-counters persistence were the sole/primary blocker (it visibly still does at line 608's summary phrasing and the table row at line 672, even though section 0 above it already supersedes that framing) -- and correct ISS-0402.yaml's own status to reflect this is a deliberate not-now scoping decision, not an unresolved code defect. No CODE-DESIGNER design work and no ELIXIR-DEV code change is warranted; branch-level cancellation as a caller-facing feature would need a brand-new requirement (out of WF-03's scope) once the two semantic questions above get a product answer.
issues: req052-instance-cancellation.md's section-4 prose (line 608 summary) and its cross-reference table (line 672) still read as if join-counters persistence were OQ-2's whole/primary reason, even though section 0's own 2026-08-22 update already supersedes that framing with the stronger R-Co-parity finding (ISS-0098). This internal inconsistency is what let ISS-0402 be filed against a stale framing in the first place, and would let a third re-litigation happen again unless corrected.

docs/issues/ISS-0402.yaml's own scoping_note (from the 20260902 run) already reached this identical conclusion and recommended closing the queue task; this run independently re-confirms it from a fresh read of current HEAD. gate_history.notes: Re-diagnosis from fresh reads of design doc, engine.ex, and ISS-0098/ISS-0397 confirms the prior 20260902 conclusion: join-counters persistence gap is genuinely closed, but an independent, already-on-record R-Co-parity reason (ISS-0098) makes whole-instance-only cancellation intentional, not a stopgap. Verdict: doc-only correction (update OQ-2's framing in req052-instance-cancellation.md and ISS-0402.yaml's status), not new design or implementation work. Routed to ORCH.
